route.rationale: write guard refuses absolute Bash targets after cd; guard source is a judge-required root

cells.title: Check absolute write targets after a cd instead of refusing them
cells.action: Keep contract d199ac87 (guard-cd-absolute-targets). In write_guard/guards.rs extract_bash_targets, mark a target cd-opaque only when its index is at or after the cd marker AND std::path::Path::new(target).is_absolute() is false; an absolute target after a cd is then resolved and checked by main.rs exactly like a target with no cd. Targets before a cd and relative targets after a cd keep their current behavior; a ~ path stays relative here. Red first in write_guard/tests.rs: extend or add extractor tests named with cd_ so the filter runs them (an absolute target after cd is not opaque, a relative one is, mixed commands mark per target), and fixture tests named with cd_ through the existing bash()/expect_done helpers: cd /tmp && touch <fixture root absolute path to an ordinary in-root file> is allowed; cd /tmp && touch <fixture root absolute path>/.bee/state.json is refused with the direct-edit wording and never the cd wording; cd /tmp && touch out.txt is still refused with the cd wording. Watch the new tests fail before the fix. Knowledge delta in the same commit: in docs/knowledge/areas/hook-runtime/write-guard-request-shapes.md change the cd bullet to say the refusal applies to relative targets only and an absolute target after a cd is checked normally, citing docs/history/guard-cd-absolute-targets/CONTEXT.md D1 (not the raw decision id). No code comments. One commit.

truths: An absolute write target after a cd is resolved and checked like a target with no cd
A relative write target after a cd is still refused with the cd wording
An absolute target after a cd that hits a guarded bee state file is still refused

artifacts.substantive: red-first tests for absolute and relative targets after cd

key_links: main.rs refuses only targets that guards.rs marks cd_opaque
prohibitions: Never skip containment or direct-edit checks for an absolute target
